chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Yaqub ibn Yazid, from Ibrahim ibn Abi Samak, from Ali ibn Shahab ibn Abdeh Rabbeh, from his father, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The donors are three: God, the Lord of the Worlds; the owner of the property; and the one who acts as the intermediary through whose hands it is distributed.

key_terms.يُجْرِي عَلَى يَدَيْهِ: Acts as intermediary / Through whose hands it is distributed

ai.seo_question: Who are the three donors in Islamic charity according to this hadith?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq categorizes the 'donors' into the Divine Source (Allah), the material owner, and the distributive intermediary, reflecting the Shia emphasis on the chain of blessing in charity. This triad underscores that while God is the ultimate Giver, human agency in ownership and distribution is spiritually significant and rewarded. The classification serves to elevate the status of the distributor, linking their action directly to the divine will.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 3-146 Muhammad ibn al-Hassan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Hassan al-Saffar quoted Yaqoob ibn Yazid, on the authority of Ibrahim ibn Abi Samak, on the authority of Ali ibn Shahab ibn Abdeh Rab’beh, on the authority of his father that Aba Abdullah as-Sadiq (MGB) said,
“There are three donors: God - the Lord of the Two Worlds: those who own the property given for charity; and those who act as mediators for charity.”
